_doc: Rules for German output. The German CV is not produced by translating at render time: reviewed German text lives in career.json as text_de beside each English bullet, and render.py only looks it up. A translation generated fresh on every run is not reviewable, and hard rule 2 requires every claim to be traceable to something a human checked.
_why_this_file_exists: German job titles carry legal weight that English ones do not. A careless translation does not merely read badly, it claims a credential. This is the list of what must never appear, and the wording approved instead.

never_use.reason: Protected by the Landesingenieurgesetze. Using it without the qualification is not a stylistic choice, it is a false claim. Applies to compounds too: Softwareingenieur, Trainingsingenieur.
never_use.instead: Entwickler, or leave the original English title

never_use.reason: Implies the AEVO certificate and a role in the formal dual training system. He is a corporate trainer, which is a different thing.
A specific qualification with an examination behind it.
An academic degree prefix he does not hold.

never_use.instead: Dozent for adult education, Trainer for corporate

never_use.reason: Fine in compounds like Kundenberater. Avoid alone where it could read as Steuerberater or Rechtsberater, both regulated.

job_titles.rule: Titles held at international employers stay in the language they were held in. That is conventional on German CVs for such employers, and it removes the protected-title problem at source.
examples: Global Enablement Content Lead, Mimecast GmbH
Principal Technical Education Consultant, Symantec (Deutschland) GmbH

approved_terms.enablement: Enablement is used untranslated in German corporate settings and is clearer than Befähigung
approved_terms.training: Schulung for a course, Training for the ongoing activity
approved_terms.onboarding: Einarbeitung for staff, Onboarding for customers
approved_terms.customer success: Customer Success, untranslated, as the industry uses it

mechanical_rules: Hyphenated compounds are wrapped in a nowrap span by render.py. A line break on the hyphen makes pdftotext drop it, so Enablement-Programm extracts as EnablementProgramm and a parser indexes a word that does not exist. ats_check verifies every compound in the source survived.
German runs roughly twenty percent longer than English, so the same content overflows. --since 2013 holds two bullets per role at two pages; without it the fit falls to one.
No em dashes, per profile/writing-style.md. German uses them even more freely than English, so this needs watching in translated text.
No photo and no date of birth, per his standing rule, even though German convention still expects both. This is a deliberate choice, not an oversight.
_review_status: The 28 German bullets in career.json were drafted 2026-09-18 and have not been read by a native speaker. He is fluent spoken, so reading them aloud will catch anything that sounds wrong. Nothing here should go to an employer before that.
